data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, who complete both treatment visits with evaluable primary outcome) Summary measure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018); non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval of the paired difference is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from the efficacy analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, including adverse events, withdrawal of consent, or investigator decision

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient's lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, meaning hypoglycemia was not adequately induced and the primary outcome is non-evaluable

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, who complete both treatment visits with evaluable primary outcome
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018); non-inferiority declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval of the paired difference is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, and summary statistics for vital signs, presented by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study treatment or withdraws from the study due to an adverse event prior to completing both treatment periods

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications for adverse event management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications to manage treatment-emergent adverse events such as nausea, vomiting, or allergic reactions during the study

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of serious adverse events (SAEs), treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal adverse events, and changes in vital signs
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, and summary statistics for vital signs, presented by treatment group

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PK samples (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; additional comparative analyses as specified in the statistical analysis plan.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete PK blood samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or incomplete serial blood samples for PK assessment due to sampling difficulties, patient withdrawal, or protocol deviations

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling window
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or is withdrawn before completion of the 4-hour post-dose PK blood sampling window

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed glucagon concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax) derived from serial blood sampling immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; additional comparative analyses as specified in the statistical analysis plan

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD data. Data collected after receipt of IV glucose infusion to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia may be excluded. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters including BGmax and Tmax by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other intervention to raise PG concentration after glucagon administration; measurements taken after the time of intervention will be excluded from the PD analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete PD blood samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or incomplete serial plasma glucose samples for PD assessment due to sampling difficulties, patient withdrawal, or protocol deviations

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose compared to 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen) administered as a single IM injection, in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters including maximum plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax) derived from serial plasma glucose measurements immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters including BGmax and Tmax by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized by treatment group

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable antibody samples collected at follow-up (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment) or does not provide a blood sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before follow-up visit
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient withdraws consent or is lost to follow-up before the scheduled antibody assessment at the follow-up visit

data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation
data.variableOfInterest: Presence of anti-glucagon antibodies assessed at the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after the last study treatment)
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts and percentages of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics for baseline, various post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline in total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not complete the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale questionnaire at one or more scheduled assessment time points due to clinical condition, withdrawal, or other reasons
